messages:
Maya: heads-up :rotating_light: - we're seeing a p99 latency regression on nyx-1.2 after the tokenizer switch. started ~2024-03-21 21:10 UTC. affected route: /v1/generate (nyx-1.2). p95 ~1.2s -> 2.0s, p99 ~1.3s -> 4.9s for sequences >8192 tokens. customers hitting timeouts and retries. example request-id: rcv-20240321-9a2f. posting logs and a minimal repro below.

Devon: @Maya can you attach a sample request and the job id from the runtime traces? also which pool (shared/dedicated)?

Maya: shared-hosted us-west-2. sample payload (trimmed):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"nyx-1.2","input":"<~8k tokens of chat history>...","max_tokens":512}'
```

response headers: 
`X-Request-Id: rcv-20240321-9a2f`
`x-route: /v1/generate`

Devon: thanks. Can you also paste token counts from the console for that request? suspecting tokenizer expansion.

Maya: grabbed from the debug endpoint: `/debug/tokenize?model=nyx-1.2` for the payload -> tokens_in: 8320, tokens_out_estimate: 3832, tokenized_length: 11340 (!!!). previous model nyx-1.1 for same payload -> tokenized_length: 8421. So nyx-1.2 tokenization step is increasing token count by ~35%.

Sam: that matches my local repro of the bpe-merge-v3 changes. New merge rules changed boundary heuristics for long CJK/emoji sequences and introduced extra split points. Extra tokens blow up KV cache indexing and cause more cache misses + higher memory pressure per request which increases latency.

Nora: do we have a diff/commit on the tokenizer that landed? who authored?

Sam: commit `bpe-merge-v3` landed in nyx-1.2 build. author @liam. It passed unit tests but long-sequence perf wasn't covered.

Liam: yep that was my change. I added finer-grain merges to improve generation quality for multilingual input. I didn't expect the token count delta to be that large on pathological long-context inputs. shoulder-slap from me.

Maya: mitigation suggestions from support ops so far: 1) pin affected customers to nyx-1.1 2) add runtime flag `tokenizer_mode=legacy` for nyx-1.2 that uses previous merge table 3) temporary autoscale/burst to dedicated capacity (expensive) 4) roll back the bpe merge in the next nyx patch. which ones do we want to pursue immediately?

Devon: short-term: pin to nyx-1.1 for the impacted customers and create an automated route rule for similar high-longcontext requests. medium-term: a rollback patch for nyx-1.2 or shipping `tokenizer_mode=legacy`.

EngRuntime-Bot: incident created: INC-20240321-1429 - "nyx-1.2 tokenizer expansion causing p99 spike". Linked traces: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20240321-1429

Sam: repro steps I used locally: 
1) curl debug tokenize to measure tokenized_length:
```bash
curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/debug/tokenize?model=nyx-1.2' -d @long_payload.txt 
# returns tokenized_length: 11340
```
2) hit the runtime with the same payload via a small load test (5 concurrent clients, 1 RPS each) for 30s -> p99 jumps to 4.6s and errors start after 60s due to memory pressure.

Maya: known impact list: 3 enterprise customers reported (acct A, B, C). customer A: retries caused duplicated expensive billing events, billing flagged it. I've looped in finance and support.

Liam: I can prepare a quick patch to revert the merge table and cut nyx-1.2.1 that restores original tokenization behavior. ETA ~2–3 hours if we prioritize. Alternatively I can expose a `tokenizer_mode` flag which is slightly more work (~1 day).

Nora: Ops ask: can we temporarily apply a per-customer routing rule to send any request with header `X-Context-Length > 8000` to nyx-1.1? That would be the fastest fix without rollback.

Devon: yes, we have routing predicate support. I can set a canary rule for the 3 impacted accounts within 10–15m. Will monitor p99.

Maya: please do that and post the rule id and the change. Also enable `prefix_cache=true` on the route for nyx-1.1 so their long histories reuse KV caches.

Devon: rule created: `route-20240321-nyx-longctx-pin-001`. Predicate: header `X-Account-Id in [A,B,C] OR X-Context-Length > 8000`. Action: route -> nyx-1.1, prefix_cache=true. Deployed to us-west-2 shared pool.

MonitoringBot: after routing rule, p99 for the affected accounts dropped from 4.9s -> 1.4s within 5m. overall shared pool p99 reduced by ~0.6s.

Maya: :thumbsup: good. Next steps:
- Liam to prepare rollback patch (nyx-1.2.1) or `tokenizer_mode` plan.
- Sam to add a regression test that runs tokenization diffs on long-context corpora (>=16k chars) and checks token expansion delta < 10%.
- Devon to keep routing rule for 24–48h, then gradually remove after patch is deployed and verified.
- Support to reconcile billing duplicates with finance for customer A.

Liam: starting rollback now. I'll open PR and request an expedited review.

Sam: will add CI job and throw some long-CJK/emoji fixtures into the tokenization test harness.

Nora: finance looped in, support sent credits to customer A as a short-term remediation.

Maya: closing the customer-facing escalation thread once nyx-1.2.1 is released and customers confirm. tagging eng-runtime for postmortem and adding an action item to add long-context perf tests in onboarding checklist for new tokenizers.

Devon: note for postmortem: also track any cost delta from routing to older model and dedicated bursts.

EngRuntime-Bot: update: PR `revert-bpe-merge-v3` opened: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/nyx/pull/492 - CI started.

Maya: thanks everyone. will keep thread updated with release and customer confirmations.

Liam: PR green, deploying patch to staging now. will coordinate canary and then prod after 30m of staging health.

MonitoringBot: staging canary metrics: p99 back to baseline for nyx-1.2.1 -> 1.25s. no memory pressure observed.

Maya: once deployed to prod, we'll notify customers and close INC-20240321-1429.

Devon: prod deploy scheduled in 45m. I'll keep rollback window 2h.

Nora: customer A confirmed they see normal latency in our test app. support closing their ticket in 24h.

Maya: Incident resolved after release. Summary for postmortem: tokenizer merge heuristic change caused ~35% token expansion for certain long-context inputs which led to higher KV cache miss/BW and memory pressure, increasing p99. Immediate mitigation: per-customer routing to nyx-1.1 + revert patch nyx-1.2.1. Action items: add long-context tokenization perf tests to onboarding, expose `tokenizer_mode` for safer rollouts, update deployment checklist for tokenizers.

Devon: noted. Will start the postmortem doc and link action items to the incident.
